_README: R252 / report #118 — THE GAME'S OWN WORDS FOR THE MARKERS NO CARD REMINDS YOU ABOUT.
R248 gave every glossary row two audiences: `text` is what a PLAYER reads and
`rule` is what the REPOSITORY states. It filled `text` from the pool's own
`{i}(...)` reminder spans, which covers 15 of the 43 rows. The other 28 kept the
repo's authored generalisation on screen — and that is what the owner objected
to next: {Virus} and {Augment} print no reminder on any card, so a player was
still reading our sentence and not the game's.
This file is the SECOND channel: the Algomancy Manual, which is the game's own
rules document and the top of Rules/README.md's authority order. Seven rows are
in it. The other twenty-one are not, and that is recorded rather than papered
over: test/231-manual-text.test.ts pins, per row, whether the manual has no
entry at all or an entry that cannot be quoted cleanly.
HOW TO AUDIT A ROW. Every `text` below is a VERBATIM contiguous run of the
manual, de-hyphenated across its line breaks and nothing else. Open the PDF at
the `page` given, find the `heading`, and read. You are not required to trust
this file: 231 rebuilds each sentence out of the fragments of the checked-in
Rules/Algomancy-Manual.txt, in increasing line order, and fails if a single
word was paraphrased. Its positive controls are a reworded sentence and an
invented one, and both must stay red.
WHAT MAY GO IN HERE. A contiguous run of manual prose under a heading that
NAMES the term — 231 asserts the heading really does, so the rule is machine-
checked and not a promise. That rule is what keeps this from becoming a second
authored table assembled out of the manual's words, and it is why two rows that
LOOK extractable are not here:
· {Graft}'s defining sentence reads 'denoted by the      or      symbol' once
the two glyphs drop out of text extraction. A half-captured sentence shown
as if it were the rulebook is worse than our own honest one.
· {Unstable} is defined under the heading PERMADEATH (p.35), which does not
name it, and only for the modded route — it would tell a player that
Aberrant Statweaver and Oorblak, which PRINT the attribute on their type
line, do not have it, and it is silent on R145's active-zone scope. Both
omissions are ones R206/CT-80 had to put back once already.
WHAT MAY NOT. Shortening a row. The authored sentence is never edited and never
deleted — `asShown` MOVES it to `rule`, exactly as it does for a printed
reminder, and 177 §7 asserts it arrives there character for character. For the
twenty rows with no manual entry the authored sentence is still the only
statement of the rule this repository has (R206 / CT-80), so it stays on screen.
